column1: ## Resistance loci in BX571856.1 (S. aureus MRSA252)
## Coordinates taken from the EMBL feature table of BX571856.1 itself, not
## from a secondary annotation. Five of the six agree exactly with BV-BRC
## genome 282458.100; grlB does not (ENA starts at 1417763, BV-BRC at
## 1417769 -- a 6 bp difference in the start-codon call). ENA wins here,
## since Gordon et al. numbered against this record.
## fusA carries no /gene qualifier in the EMBL record; it is tagged `fus`
## (SAR0552). Found by product ("translation elongation factor G").
## Translation of all six was verified against the genome FASTA: every CDS
## begins at a start codon, ends in a stop, and contains no internal stops.
## grlA and rpoB begin with V and L respectively -- GTG/TTG starts, normal
## in S. aureus, not an off-by-one.
## !! MRSA252 IS ITSELF QUINOLONE-RESISTANT !!
## The reference already carries three resistance alleles from the Gordon
## catalogue:
##     gyrA S84L      grlA S80F      grlB P451S
## At these codons the reference base IS the resistant state. A pipeline
## that calls resistance by "variant differs from reference" will therefore
## report every SUSCEPTIBLE sample as resistant at these positions, and stay
## silent on genuinely resistant ones. The logic must be
## "what amino acid does this sample actually have", never "does it differ
## from MRSA252". See ref_is_resistant below and how 08_call_resistance.py
## uses it.
## Columns:
##   gene        catalogue gene name
##   locus_tag   BX571856.1 locus tag
##   start,end   1-based inclusive, on the forward strand of BX571856.1
##   strand      + or -; dfrB is on the minus strand
##   aa_length   including the terminal stop
##   drug        what Gordon's table predicts from this gene
